sources.citation: Richardson, Dan & Ian Tupper. 2013. The cases of Sos Kundi and Ambakich: drawing language boundaries and assigning names. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2013-005. Dallas: SIL International. 21 pp. (Glottolog reference 116723.)
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: Nothing on stress or tone for any variety: the report covers speakers' boundary perceptions, a 170-item wordlist lexicostatistic comparison (14 Sos Kundi villages, Keak data from the 2005 Malinguat survey, one Iatmul list from Namuk) and intelligibility; the only prosody-adjacent words are informants' Tok Pisin remarks glossed 'it's a different accent/they sound slightly different' (p. 7). 'Burui' does not occur in the text (a full-text search for stress/accent 0). sources.citation: Aikhenvald, Alexandra Y. 2008. The Manambu language of East Sepik, Papua New Guinea. Oxford: OUP. Ch.1, note 3 (Ndu languages overview).
sources.note: Nothing on Burui stress. Identity only: '(Burui, Maligwat, and Gaikundi, listed as separate Ndu languages on the Ethnologue website, are among the Iatmul dialects.).. of these, Sengo, Burui, Kwaruwi Kundi, and also Gaikundi appear to be members of the Iatmul continuum.' Refers to Staalsen (1975) for the Sawos reappraisal.

sources.citation: Carrington, Lois. 1996. A linguistic bibliography of the New Guinea area. Pacific Linguistics D-90. Canberra: Australian National University. xiii+476 pp.
sources.note: nothing; bibliographic index only. Confirms that as of 1996 no manuscript or publication specific to Burui (beyond Staalsen 1975's survey coverage of the Sawos region) was known to Pacific Linguistics.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1973. Sepik languages: checklist and preliminary classification. Pacific Linguistics B-25. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Village-by-village assignment of Burui (Sawos vs Iatmul) for the identity question; open on sealang.net but unreachable today.

sources.citation: Staalsen, Philip. 1969. The dialects of Iatmul. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 10, Pacific Linguistics A-22: 69-84.
sources.note: No mention of Burui found (scanned a full-text search for stress/accent with spacing-tolerant pattern); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1965. The Ndu language family (Sepik District, New Guinea). Pacific Linguistics C-1. Canberra: ANU. Sec. 14 'Notes on the Sawos language', pp.143-144; sec. 18.24.
sources.note: Nothing for Sawos/Burui: 'it was not possible to elicit material in Sawos' (14.13); only two Tolembei speakers met; Burui village not named. No Sawos phonology at all.
